c.tagline: A sun-warmed Hungarian city of Ottoman-era mosques, Zsolnay ceramics, and Roman-era tombs beneath its streets

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis have yellow plates and roof signs; confirm the meter is running or agree a fare in advance, especially from the train station

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number; Hungary's older direct lines (107 police, 104 ambulance, 105 fire) also still work

hood_landmark.Belváros: Pécs Cathedral & Mosque of Pasha Qasim

hood_desc: Pécs' walkable historic core, centered on Széchenyi Square and the former Ottoman-era Pasha Qasim Mosque. Cobbled lanes lead to Pécs Cathedral, the Zsolnay Fountain, and the city's best cafés and shops.

The beautifully restored 19th-century Zsolnay porcelain factory grounds, now a cultural quarter of museums, galleries, and design shops. It's the best place to see the manufacturer's famous iridescent eosin glaze up close.

A leafy hillside above downtown with the ruins of a 16th-century Ottoman garden pavilion and sweeping views over Pécs' rooftops. Quiet trails and a small chapel make it a favorite for an evening walk.
A mostly residential district of socialist-era apartment blocks built for uranium-mining families in the 1950s-60s. It offers a glimpse of everyday, non-touristy Pécs with local markets and parks.
A newer suburban district on the city's edge with shopping centers and family housing. Handy for practical errands but with little of historic interest.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Hungary.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5am-11pm, reduced frequency on weekends
transit.pay: Single tickets bought on board or from machines; multi-day passes available
transit.note: The historic center is compact and best explored on foot; buses mainly serve outlying districts

air: Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (BUD) - main gateway, ~200km away
Pécs-Pogány Airport (PEV) - tiny local airport with very limited seasonal flights
train: Direct trains to/from Budapest, roughly 2.5-3 hours
bus: Volánbusz coaches connect Pécs with Budapest and regional towns

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving about 10% in restaurants is customary when service is good; not expected for taxis or small purchases

landmarks: Early Christian Necropolis of Sopianae
A UNESCO World Heritage complex of fourth-century painted burial chambers beneath the cathedral square, unrivalled outside Italy for Roman Christian art.
Mosque of Pasha Qasim
A domed Ottoman mosque dominating the main square, converted into a Catholic church yet still crowned by both cross and crescent.
Pécs Cathedral
The four-towered Romanesque-revival Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul, whose 11th-century crypt and frescoed chapels anchor the city's episcopal quarter.
Zsolnay Cultural Quarter
The revitalised factory campus of the famed Zsolnay porcelain dynasty, mixing museums, iridescent eosin ceramics, ateliers and gardens.
Széchenyi Square
Pécs' sloping Mediterranean-feeling main square, ringed by pastel facades and centred on the mosque, plague column and ornate Zsolnay Fountain.
Barbican
A rotund 15th-century bastion tower with a drawbridge, the most picturesque surviving piece of the medieval bishop's-castle walls.
Csontváry Museum
A gallery devoted to visionary painter Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka, whose vast canvases of Taormina and Baalbek mesmerised even Picasso.
Jakováli Hasszán Mosque
Hungary's best-preserved Ottoman mosque, still retaining its slender minaret and serving as an evocative reminder of 143 years of Turkish rule.
Pécs Synagogue
A grand Romantic-style synagogue of 1869 on Kossuth Square, its painted ceilings and organ testifying to the city's once-flourishing Jewish community.
Misina TV Tower
A 197-metre lookout tower atop the Mecsek hills, its observation deck surveying the red rooftops of Pécs and the vineyards beyond.

intl.to: Osijek (Croatia) - via Magyarbóly and Beli Manastir, with onward connections towards Sarajevo; check current status

train.note: Pecs station stands on Szabadsag ut about 1.5 km south of the main square, with frequent MAV-START trains from Budapest Deli and Keleti taking as little as 2 hr 40 min on the fastest workings. The cross-border link south to Osijek in Croatia runs via Magyarboly and Beli Manastir and has historically been a single daily service with onward connections towards Sarajevo, but it has been suspended and reinstated repeatedly, so confirm it on jegy.mav.hu before planning around it. Domestic tickets can be bought right up to departure, while international fares are cheaper booked ahead and the window opens roughly two months out. Hungary and Croatia are both in Schengen now, so the crossing is a formality, though ID checks still happen.

bus.note: The bus station (Autobuszallomas) is right beside the railway station and is served by Volanbusz (https://www.volanbusz.hu/), whose coaches run many times a day to Budapest Nepliget - slower and less comfortable than the train, and worth it mainly for the fare. Regional services fan out across Baranya county to Harkany, Siklos, Mohacs and the Villany wine villages. Tickets come from the office, the driver or the MAV-Volan group website. No international coach starts in Pecs: FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) and the other cross-border operators run from Budapest Nepliget, about three hours away.

ferry.note: Pecs is an inland city tucked under the Mecsek hills with no river of its own. The Danube is 30-40 km east at Mohacs, where there is a car ferry across the river and where international river cruises call, but nothing scheduled connects to Pecs itself. Hungary's passenger boat services, run by Mahart PassNave (https://www.mahartpassnave.hu/), operate on the Danube out of Budapest and on Lake Balaton, both well to the north.

half.name: Villány
half.blurb: A wine village about 30 minutes south is known for red wine cellars carved into hillsides and a wine museum on its main street.

half.name: Siklós
half.blurb: A hilltop castle town roughly 40 minutes south holds Hungary's oldest continuously inhabited castle, now housing a museum and wax figure exhibit.

half.name: Harkány
half.blurb: A thermal spa town about 25 minutes south draws visitors to sulfurous outdoor pools said to ease rheumatic and skin conditions.

half.name: Orfű
half.blurb: A cluster of lakes in the Mecsek hills about 20 minutes from Pécs offers swimming, a water mill, and a mining and forestry museum.

half.name: Mohács
half.blurb: A Danube river town about an hour southeast marks the site of the 1526 battle where Ottoman forces defeated the Hungarian kingdom's army.
